description: This schematic map illustrates a coastal lagoon environment, detailing various land cover types and their spatial arrangement. The legend defines five categories: "Coastal lagoon" (light blue), "Sand bank" (yellow), "Reed beds and marsh plants" (grey areas with green vertical plant symbols), "Sea and ocean" (dark blue), and "Irrigated land" (light green). The main body of water, a coastal lagoon, is depicted in light blue and is connected to the dark blue "Sea and ocean" on the right side by a narrow, elongated yellow "Sand bank". The coastal lagoon is extensively surrounded by light green "Irrigated land" to its left and top. Within the coastal lagoon and along its edges, several distinct areas of "Reed beds and marsh plants" are shown in grey with green plant symbols, marked with labels A, B, C, and D. Area A is a smaller patch of reed beds and marsh plants within the lagoon. Areas B and C are larger, more complex formations of reed beds and marsh plants situated along the interface between the irrigated land and the lagoon on the left side. Area D is a smaller, isolated patch of reed beds and marsh plants on the top right, bordering both the irrigated land and the coastal lagoon.
